title: Carried Forward, Unopened, Explained
subtitle: Hedvig Anyanwu on what an office fits into its crates when it moves, and what the crates nobody opens carry to the next move
summary: A research explainer from the School of Emergent Priorities on Hedvig Anyanwu's doctoral thesis about the crates an office packs when it moves. It follows a public-sector agency's move to a new building, where fifty-seven crates packed for its previous relocation went across with the rest, still unopened, and most of them on through its next move fourteen months later. Anyanwu describes the packing-day inventory and the carried-forward crates she opened at the end of fieldwork herself, the film sets out the packing-day protocol her School has adopted for its own priority-setting, and a sentence from her thesis, in her own voice, closes it.
topic: A research explainer of the doctoral thesis following crates through four office restacks at three organisations, from a packing-day inventory of 21,946 items to a public-sector agency's second restack, at which 118 crates moved unopened, 55 of them packed for its relocation in 2017, finding that workers gave up items in current use to close a lid while keeping material from ended programs, and that discontinued material made up 36.2% of the carried-forward crates opened at the end of fieldwork, nearly three times its share at packing, and closing on the packing-day protocol the School of Emergent Priorities has adopted from 2027
